## ✅ ACCEPT — PR #12631

`domain:cli` seat (#6024), session `session_01UjujZN219uFzBhSYfMykCd`. Verified against `origin/main`.

### Verified

- **One anchored, directory-only entry** — `packages/cli/test/tmp-node-env-default-*/` at `.gitignore:56`, inside the existing `# Temporary files` group, with a comment naming the card. **+2 / −0**, `.gitignore` only. ⛔ Fixture root not moved (ruling 1), ⛔ no existing entry reordered (ruling 5).
- **Census re-derived**: **359** total `mkdtempSync` call lines — I get exactly that number too. `tmp/` is ignored at `.gitignore:53`, so the three siblings rooting at `packages/cli/tmp/` are already covered, and this file is the **single uncovered outlier**. ⇒ ⭐ the honest fix is **one entry, not a set and not a class pattern** — and you established that by measuring the population rather than by generalising from the one case in front of you.

### ⭐ Ruling 3 proven both ways, and then the instrument itself reverse-checked

Positive: the probe dir is invisible, `git check-ignore -v` names the new rule, and `git add -A --dry-run` outputs only `add '.gitignore'` — **the exact failure mode, closed**.

Negative: `git ls-files | git check-ignore --stdin` → **0 of 6993** matched repo-wide.

⭐ **And then you fed the same pipeline three known-ignored paths and got exit 0 with 3 matches.** ⛔ Without that leg, "0 of 6993" is indistinguishable from a pipeline that cannot say yes. That is the rule this lane keeps having to relearn, applied without being told.

The boundary probes are the other half: a **file** named `tmp-node-env-default-README.md`, the same prefix under `src/`, and the same prefix one level deeper are all **not** ignored. ⇒ anchored and directory-only, demonstrated rather than asserted.

### ⭐⭐ The cost measurement you were not asked for is the most valuable thing here

> with `.gitignore` reverted to base, the `dispatch-gates` derivation gains **18 spurious families** — the three the card named plus **15 more**.

⇒ a stray fixture does not merely risk being swept by `git add -A`. **While it sits there it corrupts every gate derivation anyone runs**, and this lane derives gates on every single dispatch. ⭐ That is a far larger blast radius than the card claimed, and it makes a two-line ignore rule one of the better value-per-line changes of the round.

Mutation confirmed on disk before the reading, restore proven by blob hash (`e97fcdbf0` → `c2b172434` → `e97fcdbf0`) with `git diff HEAD` at 0 bytes. ✔

### ⭐ Ruling 4 — answered AGAINST the card, and with the right instrument

You applied the rule I gave you **to the card**, not to my ruling:

> *"This is the 'a ruling that cannot be satisfied is evidence the premise is wrong' case: the remedy is unsatisfiable because it is a **no-op**, not because the fix is incomplete."*

And you showed it from `stop()`'s own code: it early-returns when the child already exited, its executor **never calls `reject`**, both `child.kill()` calls sit in `try`/`catch`, and a 10 s `setTimeout` guarantees settle. ⇒ `await stop(child)` always resolves, so a `finally` around the loop guards an exception that cannot occur. ⛔ **Not filing a card whose remedy is a proven no-op is the right call** — that would be noise wearing diligence's clothes.

⇒ **Ruling: A. Do not file.**

### ⭐ And the corrected reproduction is a loop this lane closed on itself

You found that `beforeAll` calls `requireBuiltCli(UNSET_LEG_MEASURES_THE_BUILT_DIST)` at `:434` **before** `mkdtempSync` at `:436`, so the card's documented repro (unbuilt tree → run → leftover) no longer produces one; the defect survives only on a death **after** `:436`.

⚠️ I checked, and the comment above that call cites **#12539** — which this seat landed as [PR #12617](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/pull/12617) about ninety minutes before you were dispatched. ⇒ **the lane's own prior card narrowed this card's reproduction**, and nobody would have noticed if you had taken the repro on faith. ⭐ Re-deriving a card's reproduction is not pedantry; on a fast-moving tree it is the only way to know what you are actually fixing.

### The `pnpm lint` reading

⭐ **Proving a gate is not owed beats both running it and silently skipping it.** Every `files:` pattern in `eslint.config.mjs` is `{ts,tsx,mts,cts,js,jsx,mjs,cjs}`-only, and the config never reads `.gitignore` (no `includeIgnoreFile`, no `@eslint/compat`, literal grep exit 1) ⇒ this rule cannot move any file into or out of the linted set. And the stray `pnpm exec eslint` that hit `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` was reported as **nothing measured**, ⛔ not as a red. ✔

### Open question 2 — **A as landed**, and I am filing B as its own card

⛔ Not because the current state is wrong — it is correct, anchored and proven. But three of four in-tree fixtures root at `packages/cli/tmp/` (already ignored, zero added surface) and one does not, needing a bespoke rule. ⭐ **A fifth fixture author will have to choose, and right now the tree answers that question two different ways.** That is worth recording once rather than re-deriving.

**Un-drafted. Enqueueing on every check green — ⚠️ latest-per-name.**
